html:
Kaw (Oklahoma) marks the land of the Kaw Nation in north central Oklahoma, around Kaw City and Newkirk. The Kaw, or Kansa, a Dhegiha Siouan people, were moved here from Kansas in 1873; see Kaw for their earlier history.

Their reservation in Indian Territory was divided into private allotments in 1902. In the 1970s the Kaw Dam flooded their old town of Washunga and its council grounds, and the council house was moved to Kaw City. The Kaw Nation keeps its government there today, next to the lands of the Osage.
